# OpenAI Codex adapter

**Verified coverage (2026-11-06):** Cold reviewer and investigator dispatch was verified with Codex CLI 0.166.0, AIVV plugin 0.3.0, and profiles generated by the installer. A desktop-native question exchange confirmed the exact scope and method of a general review of a disposable non-code plan; the cold review completed with the fixture unchanged. Review/calibration publication, schema validation, viewer readback, and fresh-process lookup by target were verified. A reliable target store containing an earlier review was rediscovered after a desktop restart without a cached context.

**Boundaries:** Uncertain filesystem identities intentionally use session-local stores; recover those records with their saved `--context` / `--storage-context` handle rather than silently adopting them by path. The desktop test verified the submitted native question response and review execution; Computer Use cannot inspect Codex, so automated visual inspection was not performed. Hook trust is controlled by the user and was not tested.

Install the plugin from Codex CLI:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add iliaim/AIVV --ref main
codex plugin add aivv@aivv
```

The plugin packages AIVV skills and runtime files. Codex plugin packages do not install the custom read-only reviewer and investigator agent profiles, so cold dispatch also requires `scripts/install-codex.sh` (macOS/Linux) or `scripts/install-codex.ps1` (PowerShell). Codex skips bundled plugin hooks until a user reviews and trusts the current hook definition; review the AIVV hook files before enabling it. Keep results advisory; they are not an independent organizational or compliance audit. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/iliaim/AIVV/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for the current setup paths.

## Native model and reasoning labels

Before proposing a native review method, inspect the callable dispatch tool's
current model and reasoning-effort metadata. Use those values when describing
availability and constructing the dispatch; provider CLI settings are a separate
interface.

For the Codex native interface, the human label **extra-high** corresponds to
`xhigh`. `max` is a distinct effort value, not a substitute for extra-high.
The absence of the literal spelling `extra_high` does not mean `xhigh` is
unavailable. Preserve a requested supported value in both the proposal and the
dispatch arguments. If metadata is unavailable or the requested value is not
supported, state that limitation rather than inventing support, selecting the
highest-looking label, or silently changing the method. Apply the canonical
[scope-confirmation procedure](../../skills/aivv/references/scope-confirmation.md)
to any revised proposal.
